question_en:
Community emergency volunteers are organizing old monitoring data for a slope along a railway line. The only material available is the photo in the attachment. Please answer the following questions:

1. After locating the corresponding official time-lapse photography data, identify all clearly recorded periods of slope movement. Number them sequentially starting from P01 in chronological order. For each period of continuous movement, use the last photo taken on the day before the start date as the 'before' image and the last photo taken on the end date as the 'after' image. For events described by officials as seemingly instantaneous, use the two adjacent frames immediately before and after the event. What are the filenames, capture times, and time spans for each pair of before and after images? Which groups span from the afternoon of one day to the morning of the next day with a time interval strictly less than 18 hours? List the group numbers and their start and end dates.

Answer format: Use a table to list, by group number, the filenames, capture times, time spans, and whether each pair meets the condition of spanning overnight with less than 18 hours. The start and end dates for qualifying groups should be directly reflected in the capture time columns and do not need to be listed separately.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · P2-8-3-E02

## Step 01 · Read slope monitoring image clues

Action: Record bare soil on the slope, vegetation, monitoring cables, solar panels at the top, and the timestamp 08/20/2015 08:59 in the bottom right corner. Example query: coastal bluff landslide time lapse monitoring 2015 railway.

Evidence observation: These features are used to locate a fixed-camera monitoring sequence; the attachment does not directly identify USGS, Mukilteo, or five movement periods. The location and number of events must be determined from the description of the dataset found.

Evidence links:
https://www.usgs.gov/data/time-lapse-photography-active-coastal-bluff-landslide-mukilteo-washington-august-2015-may-2016

Result of this step: Mukilteo coastal bluff time-lapse photography data found.

## Step 02 · Lock onto official publications

Action: Read the USGS title and date range, and follow the data publication relationship to the ScienceBase record and DOI.

Evidence observation: Official data covers the active landslide in Mukilteo, Washington, with image records from 2015-08-19 to 2016-05-25; DOI is 10.5066/P99QOYL2, and ScienceBase item is 5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe.

Evidence links:
https://www.usgs.gov/data/time-lapse-photography-active-coastal-bluff-landslide-mukilteo-washington-august-2015-may-2016
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe
https://doi.org/10.5066/P99QOYL2

Result of this step: Image clues match the location, monitoring device, and time period.

## Step 03 · Read five official movement periods

Action: Extract all clearly defined movement segments from the text, sort them by occurrence time, and label continuous versus seemingly instantaneous events separately.

Evidence observation: Three multi-day segments are 2015-12-08 to 12-09, 2016-01-21 to 01-30, and 2016-03-09 to 03-14; the other two are during the nights of 2016-03-23 and 03-26, described by officials as seemingly instantaneous. P01–P05 are groupings for this question, not official filenames.

Evidence links:
https://www.usgs.gov/data/time-lapse-photography-active-coastal-bluff-landslide-mukilteo-washington-august-2015-may-2016
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe?format=json

Result of this step: The closed set consists of five events/periods; the 843 photos cannot be treated as 843 events.

## Step 04 · Obtain original image package and fixed attachment identifiers

Action: Read names, sizes, checksums, and URLs in ScienceBase files, and select the photo ZIP rather than the video containing only playback frames.

Evidence observation: Mukilteo_timelapse_photos.zip is 622116215 bytes, MD5 640f8be4c8446d79d8351faea9132027. The question package saves the ten original JPEGs used in this question without saving the entire large ZIP again; below are the exact download URLs provided by the metadata, without fabricating public URLs for individual JPEGs.

Evidence links:
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe?format=json
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/file/get/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe?f=__disk__5b%2F75%2Ff3%2F5b75f32a15f5d6e37e2c33fd6d1bbf7b2b22723e

Result of this step: Subsequent steps locate original photos by member names within the ZIP and retain the overall attachment entry point.

## Step 05 · Verify camera schedule and data gaps

Action: Review the daily shooting schedule and test frame descriptions in the official data description/FGDC metadata to explain the selection of the last afternoon frame and the next morning frame.

Evidence observation: The camera shoots daily at approximately 09:00, 12:00, and 16:00, with typical intervals of 3, 4, and 17 hours; the actual timestamps in the bottom right corner retain minutes such as 15:56–15:58. During the 2026-09-29 review, requests for the entire ZIP and adjacent frames were restricted by 403 challenges; the official schedule is corroborating evidence and cannot be presented as having re-verified the last frame of every day for all 843 frames individually.

Evidence links:
https://www.usgs.gov/data/time-lapse-photography-active-coastal-bluff-landslide-mukilteo-washington-august-2015-may-2016
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/file/get/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe?f=__disk__f5%2F3b%2F98%2Ff53b98d71aa5c228b0edd40bd850dcb64a77dc0f

Result of this step: Select frames according to existing original frames and question regulations; retain source boundaries for gaps in re-examining adjacent frames across the full sequence.

## Step 06 · Apply frame selection rules to event types

Action: For continuous segments, use the last photo taken on the day before the start date and the last photo taken on the end date; for seemingly instantaneous events, use the two adjacent frames immediately before and after the event.

Evidence observation: For P01–P03, one cannot take only the start and end moments of movement, nor can one use a full-day span for P04/P05. Officials provide the movement periods, the question provides the pairing rules, and the photos provide the filenames and timestamps; these three together constitute the answer.

Evidence links:
https://www.usgs.gov/data/time-lapse-photography-active-coastal-bluff-landslide-mukilteo-washington-august-2015-may-2016
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/file/get/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe?f=__disk__5b%2F75%2Ff3%2F5b75f32a15f5d6e37e2c33fd6d1bbf7b2b22723e

Result of this step: Establish a checklist of five groups comprising ten distinct JPEG members.

## Step 07 · Pair P01: 2015-12-08—2015-12-09

Action: Locate the before and after images from the ZIP according to this group's event type, read the year, month, day, hour, and minute in the bottom right corner respectively, and retain the official member names.

Evidence observation: Before image mukilteo-331.jpg: 2015-12-07 15:58; After image mukilteo-338.jpg: 2015-12-09 15:58. Continuous segments are paired from the last afternoon frame of the previous day to the last afternoon frame of the end date.

Result of this step: P01 time span is 48 hours; does not meet the combined condition of spanning overnight and being less than 18 hours.

## Step 08 · Pair P02: 2016-01-21—2016-01-30

Action: Locate the before and after images from the ZIP according to this group's event type, read the year, month, day, hour, and minute in the bottom right corner respectively, and retain the official member names.

Evidence observation: Before image mukilteo-465.jpg: 2016-01-20 15:57; After image mukilteo-495.jpg: 2016-01-30 15:57. Continuous segments are paired from the last afternoon frame of the previous day to the last afternoon frame of the end date.

Result of this step: P02 time span is 10 days; does not meet the combined condition of spanning overnight and being less than 18 hours.

## Step 09 · Pair P03: 2016-03-09—2016-03-14

Action: Locate the before and after images from the ZIP according to this group's event type, read the year, month, day, hour, and minute in the bottom right corner respectively, and retain the official member names.

Evidence observation: Before image mukilteo-609.jpg: 2016-03-08 15:56; After image mukilteo-627.jpg: 2016-03-14 15:56. Continuous segments are paired from the last afternoon frame of the previous day to the last afternoon frame of the end date.

Evidence links:
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/file/get/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe?f=__disk__5b%2F75%2Ff3%2F5b75f32a15f5d6e37e2c33fd6d1bbf7b2b22723e

Result of this step: P03 time span is 6 days; does not meet the combined condition of spanning overnight and being less than 18 hours.

## Step 10 · Pair P04: Night of 2016-03-23

Action: Locate the before and after images from the ZIP according to this group's event type, read the year, month, day, hour, and minute in the bottom right corner respectively, and retain the official member names.

Evidence observation: Before image mukilteo-654.jpg: 2016-03-23 15:56; After image mukilteo-655.jpg: 2016-03-24 08:56. Seemingly instantaneous events are bracketed by two adjacent frames from the previous afternoon and the next morning; do not use noon or later frames on the same day.

Evidence links:
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/file/get/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe?f=__disk__5b%2F75%2Ff3%2F5b75f32a15f5d6e37e2c33fd6d1bbf7b2b22723e

Result of this step: P04 time span is 17 hours; meets the condition of spanning from afternoon to next morning and being strictly less than 18 hours.

## Step 11 · Pair P05: Night of 2016-03-26

Action: Locate the before and after images from the ZIP according to this group's event type, read the year, month, day, hour, and minute in the bottom right corner respectively, and retain the official member names.

Evidence observation: Before image mukilteo-663.jpg: 2016-03-26 15:56; After image mukilteo-664.jpg: 2016-03-27 08:56. Seemingly instantaneous events are bracketed by two adjacent frames from the previous afternoon and the next morning; do not use noon or later frames on the same day.

Evidence links:
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/file/get/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe?f=__disk__5b%2F75%2Ff3%2F5b75f32a15f5d6e37e2c33fd6d1bbf7b2b22723e

Result of this step: P05 time span is 17 hours; meets the condition of spanning from afternoon to next morning and being strictly less than 18 hours.

## Step 12 · Independently recalculate time differences

Action: Perform time subtraction using full dates; when crossing months, calculate the number of days first, then finally check the two conditions of "next morning" and "strictly less than 18 hours".

Evidence observation: P01: December 9 at 15:58 − December 7 at 15:58 = 48 hours; P02 is 10 × 24 = 240 hours; P03 is 6 × 24 = 144 hours; for both P04 and P05, the time from 15:56 to midnight is 8 hours 04 minutes, plus another 8 hours 56 minutes, for a total of 17 hours.

Evidence links:
https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/file/get/5ef2388382ced62aaae3bbbe?f=__disk__5b%2F75%2Ff3%2F5b75f32a15f5d6e37e2c33fd6d1bbf7b2b22723e

Result of this step: Only P04 and P05 pass both screening criteria; not every instance that crosses the night qualifies.

## Step 13 · Retain video, camera layout, and catalog entries

Action: Record the video and camera location map in ScienceBase as background for positioning and monitoring, avoiding the treatment of lossy video frame extraction as original JPEGs.

Evidence observation: The video can help observe overall slope changes, and camera_location.PNG explains the monitoring layout; filenames and minute values in this question still come from the original photos. Data.gov is the catalog entry for the same publication and does not add independent events.

https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/time-lapse-photography-of-an-active-coastal-bluff-landslide-mukilteo-washington-augus-2016

Result of this step: The uses of webpages, ZIP, video, layout images, and metadata attachments are all verifiable.

## Step 14 · Verify question requirements and output scope

Action: Correspond each public mandatory item one-by-one with the above evidence, checking the total count, positive/negative items, and field formats.

Evidence observation: All five official time slots are paired; ten filenames correspond one-to-one with ten capture times, and a final table reports five groups with YES/NO. Adopt the existing original frame pairings; do not describe this round of simulation as re-acquiring the complete restricted ZIP.
